turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Hi Dana, Leo from HyperSale—uh, we help new hires ramp faster with realistic AI buyer roleplays and quote-backed scoring before they take live calls.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: We already have Gong for this. What’s meaningfully different?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Uh, Gong shows what happened after a real call; HyperSale lets reps rehearse beforehand with realistic buyers, then ties every score to their exact words.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I get the distinction. My managers don’t have time for another tool—how much work does this add for them?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Uh, reps practise independently; managers just see automatic, quote-backed scores and week-over-week improvement instead of reviewing recordings. Could we explore a pilot sometime?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: That helps. My managers rarely listen to Gong recordings, so coaching happens after deals are lost—but how would I measure whether practice actually works?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Uh, HyperSale tracks week-over-week score improvement and readiness by skill, with every score tied to exact quotes. Would a 30-day pilot be useful?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Scores alone don’t prove practice works; I’d need to see movement in ramp or live-call conversion. How would you establish that in 30 days?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Uh, we’d baseline ramp milestones and live-call conversion, then compare pilot reps with a matched group while tracking quote-backed practice gains. Could we outline that?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: That’s closer; new hires are effectively practicing on live prospects today. But we just renewed Gong, and there’s no budget this year—what would a 30-day pilot cost?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Uh, pilot pricing depends on team size and scope. Could we sketch a small cohort and revisit timing when budget opens?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: There’s no point sketching scope without a number. Give me a range for 10 new hires over 30 days—if it’s under $15k, I can sponsor it without involving the CRO.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Uh, standard pricing puts 10 reps at about $900 for a month; I’d need to confirm pilot terms. Is that workable?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: That range is workable, assuming there aren’t implementation fees. Send me something by email with confirmed terms and how you’d measure ramp and live-call conversion. I've got a meeting, I need to go.
